description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Tarrasch Trap. Never weaken with ...g6?? — develop the queen instead.

drills.briefExplanation: 8...Qd7! 9.Qc4 d5! — develop the queen, then strike in the center.
drills.description: Black to play. White recaptured 8.Nxd4 — develop 8...Qd7! and meet 9.Qc4 with 9...d5!.
drills.explanation: The antidote to the Tarrasch Trap: 8...Qd7! develops, defending d6. After 9.Qc4 Black strikes with 9...d5!, opening the center while White's queen is committed — 10.exd5 Nxd5 centralizes the knight with tempo. White's 'trap' never gets its ...g6?? trigger, and Black's active pieces give full equality. The trap needs a mistake; don't provide one.
drills.name: Queen to the Rescue

drills.briefExplanation: 6...bxc6! 7.Qd3 exd4 8.Nxd4 c5! — recapture toward the center and kick the knight at once.
drills.description: Black to play. White took on c6 — recapture with the b-pawn and strike back.
drills.explanation: An entirely different defense: 6...bxc6! recaptures toward the center, opening the b-file. After 7.Qd3 exd4 8.Nxd4 Black plays the energetic 8...c5!, kicking the knight with tempo and seizing space. White's bishop-pair advantage is neutralized by Black's central majority — a dynamic, modern way to meet the Steinitz.
drills.name: The bxc6 Alternative
